name: Airwallex
description: Airwallex is privately held and has no ticker. Review its funding rounds and valuations, its investors, and the points to confirm before buying or selling.
ledes: Airwallex is a privately held financial technology company. Its shares are not listed on an exchange and have no quoted market price; the principal public reference points are the valuations at which the company has raised capital. Its most recent financing, a $320 million Series H round announced on June 25, 2026, valued the company at $11 billion.

Founded in Melbourne in 2015, Airwallex provides businesses with multi-currency accounts, international payments, card issuing and expense management, and offers the same services to other platforms through its APIs. Existing shares change hands in privately negotiated transactions and remain subject to the company's transfer restrictions.
table_note: Valuations are as announced by the company. The Series F total of $300 million included $150 million of secondary share sales.
round_notes: Addition led the Series H, as it had the Series G. With the Series H announcement, Airwallex said its annualized revenue had reached $1.3 billion in March 2026, up 74% from a year earlier; that figure is the company's own.

A round valuation reflects the terms of the preferred stock issued in that round. Most shares sold by employees are common stock, which carries fewer rights and typically trades at a discount to the preferred price.
investors: Addition led the Series H and the Series G. Baillie Gifford, T. Rowe Price, QED Investors, Hedosophia and Amex Ventures also invested in the Series H, and Activant, Lingotto, Robinhood Ventures and TIAA Ventures joined the Series G. Other investors include DST Global, Square Peg, Salesforce Ventures, Lone Pine Capital, Visa Ventures, Blackbird, Airtree, Tencent and Sequoia Capital China.
spv_sentence: No special purpose vehicles naming Airwallex appear in SEC Form D filings.
sources: Sources: Airwallex's announcements of its Series H, Series G, Series F and Series E extension; and SEC Form D filings.
